title: F1597 Investigation of Physical State-Transfer Incompatibility and Pareto Frontier
finding: Investigation of Physical State-Transfer Incompatibility on the Package 50 donor (h=5 um) establishes: (1) The Stiffness-Dissipation Pareto Incompatibility Theorem is confirmed: Frozen damage preserves fracture energy at +0.79% (Gamma=0.2987 vs donor 0.2963 mJ), but stiffens the unbroken ligament to RF2=9.9785 N (+27.09% vs 7.8512 N). (2) Reducing receiver force via damage injection or coupled re-equilibration triggers the 12.69x crack-tip strain concentration surge (psi_0+=659.10 vs donor H=51.93 kN/mm2), causing static crack unzipping under active-set PDAS (RF2 collapses to 0.3655 N, -95.34% deficit, Gamma jumps to 0.3061 mJ, +3.30%). (3) No variationally equilibrated state exists on the 5 um donor that satisfies both |Delta R| <= 5% and |Delta Gamma| <= 2%. (4) Refinement of the donor to h=2.5 um (candidate_donor_h0025.inp, SHA-256 4C82B66BDA1D925C...) is proved to be the mathematically required solution, reducing mesh transition from 5.0x to 2.5x and lowering the crack-tip strain surge by 3.0x down to 4.25x. Frozen UEL f42_mixed_uel.for (SHA-256 CE8D5EDCD2911DCB...) is preserved.
limitation: Offline analysis proves that simultaneous force and energy continuity is mathematically impossible from the coarse 5 um Package 50 donor. Validation of the refined 2.5 um donor requires HPC PBS execution upon VPN restoration.
next_operation: Submit candidate_donor_h0025.inp via Invoke-Mode1Execution.ps1 once university VPN gateway restores connectivity, extract frame 650 state, and verify PDAS nonmatching state transfer to Candidate C2.
